name: Fan Tan (Sevens)
description: Fan Tan, also widely known as 'Sevens', 'Domino', or 'Parliament', is a classic layout-based card game where the objective is to be the first to get rid of all your cards. Players build upon a central layout of cards, starting with the Sevens and expanding outward to the Ace and Two in each suit. It is a game of both luck and light strategy, as players can choose to hold back key 'blocking' cards to prevent opponents from playing.

history.origins: Originating in the 19th century or earlier, the game has many names across different cultures: 'Parliament' in the UK, 'Domino' or 'Sevens' in many Western countries, and 'Fan Tan' (distinct from the Chinese gambling game of the same name).
timeline: 1800s: Early iterations of layout games appear in European gaming books.
1900s: Emerges as a staple family game due to its simple rules and visual layout.
Modern Era: A standard feature in digital card game collections and solitaire anthologies.
history.cultural: Used frequently as a 'filler' game or a way to teach children suit and numerical order.
history.evolution: The game's name 'Sevens' highlights its core mechanic, while 'Parliament' refers to the structured order in which cards must be played.

setup.players: 3 to 8 players. 4 to 6 is considered optimal.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack. Cards rank A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2 (Ace high).
setup.dealing: Dealer shuffles and player to dealer's right may cut. Dealer deals all cards one at a time, clockwise, starting with player to dealer's left. Some players may have one more card than others - this does not matter.

rules.objective: Be the first player to shed all cards from your hand.
rules.gameplay:
1. Starting: The player to the dealer's left (or the holder of the 7 of Diamonds in some variants) begins.
2. Valid Plays: You can only play a card if it is:
   nd A Seven (starts a new row for a suit).
   nd One higher or one lower than a card already in the layout (e.g., if the 7 of Hearts is on the table, you can play the 6 or 8 of Hearts).
3. Sequencing: Suits build up from 7 to Ace and down from 7 to 2.
4. Passing: If you cannot play a valid card, you MUST pass. In some groups, you must pay a fine (one chip) into a pot.
keyRules: No skipping: You cannot play an 8 unless the 7 of that suit is present.
Must play: If you have a legal move, you cannot pass.
Table Layout: Cards are arranged in four rows, one for each suit.

strategy.basic: Keep hold of your Sevens if you have cards at the extreme ends of that suit (Aces or 2s). By not playing the 7, you block everyone else from playing in that suit.
strategy.intermediate: Block and Release: If you have both the 6 and 8 of a suit, you control the expansion. You can hold them to prevent others from playing their 5s and 9s.
strategy.advanced: Watch the Discards: In variants where you pay a chip for passing, force your opponents to pass by withholding the midndrange cards (6s and 8s) for as long as possible.
tips: Prioritize playing cards from suits where you have many cards, as this opens up spaces for your own cards to be played.
If you are close to winning, play your 'blockers' to let the game finish before you get stuck with an endndcard.
